airport.name: Tokushima Awaodori Airport / JMSDF Tokushima Air Base

summary: Tokushima Awaodori Airport (TKS/RJOS) is a dual-use civil and military airfield in Matsushige, about 8 km north of central Tokushima. It shares its runway with JMSDF Tokushima Air Base and is named after the city's famous Awa Odori dance festival. The compact terminal handles mostly domestic flights, primarily to Tokyo Haneda, and serves as the main air gateway to eastern Shikoku.
faqs:
Q: What is the airport's official name?
A: It is officially Tokushima Awaodori Airport for civil use, while the military side is JMSDF Tokushima Air Base; both share the same runway and ICAO code RJOS.

Q: Why is it called Awaodori Airport?
A: The name references Awa Odori, Tokushima's renowned summer dance festival, and was adopted to promote the region's culture.

Q: Is Tokushima Airport a military base?
A: Yes, it is a joint civil-military airport. The Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force operates Tokushima Air Base alongside the civilian terminal, so military aircraft may be seen.

Q: How far is the airport from Tokushima Station?
A: It is roughly 8 km north of Tokushima Station, typically 25-35 minutes by airport limousine bus or taxi depending on traffic.
transport_tips: The most convenient option is the airport limousine bus to Tokushima Station (about 30 minutes) and other stops in the city; taxis are also available but cost more. Rental car counters are at the terminal, useful for exploring Naruto, the Awa Odori Kaikan, and Iya Valley. Allow extra time during the August Awa Odori festival, when roads and flights are busiest.
local_tip: Because the airfield is shared with the JMSDF, plane-spotters may occasionally see military aircraft; stay in public areas and follow any photography restrictions. Also, pick up a sudachi-flavored sweet or Naruto kintoki potato snack before security—they are local specialties.
